meta.title: CS50 AP -- taught subset (weeks 0, 3, 4, 7-9)

locator_titles.0: Week 0: Scratch -- data representation only (unary, binary, decimal, ASCII, Unicode, RGB)
locator_titles.3: Week 3: Algorithms (searching, sorting, asymptotic notation, recursion)
locator_titles.4: Week 4: Memory -- data representation only (hexadecimal, images, file I/O)

meta.caveat: Mapped from CS50 AP's own published per-week topic lists (https://cs50.harvard.edu/ap/2025/curriculum/x/weeks/<n>/), not from an audit of lecture or problem-set content -- comparable confidence to codehs_corgi, not cmu_cs1. The weeks-0-and-4 split between 'data representation' and everything else in those weeks is this teacher's own editorial cut, not a division CS50 itself draws; see cs50ap_extended for the other half.

2.1.note: Unary/binary/decimal/ASCII/Unicode/RGB (week 0) and hexadecimal (week 4) are both explicitly named -- this is DAT-1's own topic, encoding information as sequences of bits.

2.4.note: SQL is literally a program for pulling information out of a data set -- Tables, Statements, and Keywords/Functions are named week-7 topics.

3.9.note: Comparing Linear Search against Binary Search, and Bubble/Selection Sort against Merge Sort, is exactly 'compare two or more algorithms to see whether they produce the same outcome.'

3.11.note: Binary Search is a named subsection of week 3, alongside its own Shorts video.

3.17.note: Asymptotic Notation (O, Ω, Θ) is the week's own explicit framing for algorithmic efficiency.

4.1.note: Routers, TCP/IP, and DNS are named week-8 topics, with an 'Internet Primer' Short and demo ('Passing TCP/IP Packet').

5.6.note: SQL Injection Attacks are a named week-7 topic (an attack method); Sessions and Cookies (week 9) are the mechanism by which a site collects and holds data about a visitor across requests.

9-12.DA.8.note: Same representation claim as apcsp 2.1: the same image or character can be encoded more than one way (unary/binary/decimal/ASCII/Unicode/RGB, hexadecimal).

9-12.DA.9.note: SQL's own named topics -- Tables, Types, Constraints, Indexes -- are exactly 'how data is organized and where it's stored.'

9-12.NI.5.note: DNS plus routing (named week-8 topics) is literally 'how the internet looks up addresses and routes traffic.'

9-12.NI.6.note: SQL Injection Attacks, a named topic, is a concrete security threat calling for a specific defense (parameterized queries).

9-12.IC.29.note: Sessions and Cookies, named week-9 topics, are the concrete mechanism for collecting a visitor's data automatically between requests.

HS-ALG-PS-03.note: Asymptotic Notation is comparing algorithms by more than whether they're correct.

HS-DAT-DC-22.note: SQL's Types and Constraints, applied per column, are a data dictionary made explicit and enforced by the database itself.

HS-SYS-NT-34.note: Routers, TCP/IP, and DNS are the named physical/logical pieces a network diagram would show.

HS-SYS-NT-35.note: The week frames the internet as networks cooperating (Routers, TCP/IP, DNS) rather than one single network.

HS-SYS-SE-33.note: SQL Injection Attacks, paired with its standard defense (parameterized queries), is 'given a weakness, propose a fix.'

5.11.note: Base conversion -- unary/binary/decimal (week 0), hexadecimal (week 4) -- is this anchor standard by name.

5.12.note: Binary Search depends on the Boolean comparison at each step (higher/lower/found).

10.6.note: RGB (week 0) and Images/file I/O (week 4) are concrete cases of different media taking different amounts of data to represent.

C4.2.note: JavaScript (client-side), Flask (server-side), and SQL (query language) interacting is this standard's own example, and is literally how weeks 7-9 fit together.

C7.1.note: The week-8 internet primer (routers, servers, DNS) is the hardware-and-software-together claim this standard makes.

C7.5.note: Flask, with Route and Sessions, is the point where a project becomes an actually-served application rather than a local script.

C8.1.note: SQL is a full week on its own -- databases get more instructional weight here than anywhere else in this teacher's courses.

C8.2.note: Tables (a named topic) are exactly this standard's 'fields, records, tables, and views.'

C8.5.note: SQL's own Statements and Keywords/Functions are how a database gets queried and manipulated.
